summary: One story stands out: Lilly's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, released Oct 28 2026. It's the first time retatrutide has gone head-to-head with semaglutide 2 mg (Ozempic's highest approved dose) in a randomized trial. 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes. Over 80 weeks, A1C fell 2.2 points vs 1.8, and weight fell 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg) vs 9.4%. These figures assume everyone stayed on treatment. Not yet peer-reviewed. It has spread to Reuters, ABC, USA Today, NY Post, STAT, Everyday Health and more within 24 h. That meets every Lane C rule: within 48 h, a named next-gen drug, randomized, with a semaglutide arm. It is the closest thing we've had to EloraTZP. The numbers in the held L1 10-29 (2.2, 1.8, 19.5%, 20.9%) suggest it is this video. If so, re-mix it (masking 0.02 or lower, "point" restored, the drug name said correctly) and publish today rather than writing it again. A dysesthesia ('skin-sensation') Short and a Penn/JAMA Netw Open Reddit gray-market Short can follow. Second fresh hook: ACOG's first guidance on GLP-1s around pregnancy (consider stopping 1–2 months before trying to conceive) and breastfeeding (shared decision-making; avoid with preterm babies and newborns). It's now in mainstream news (WSJ Oct 28, NewsNation Oct 27). It's a strong calm Short, rated caution. The Lane A queue gets fresh hooks this week: bones and muscle (Arch Osteoporos review, J Clin Med device-measured muscle, Omada muscle share), stopping (Medscape on support tools after GLP-1s, Oct 28), hair loss (Medscape, similar risk across races, Oct 28), and plateaus (Diabetes Obes Metab 12-month real-world tirzepatide, Oct 28). Seasonal: 'food noise' before Halloween (Psychiatric Times, Oct 28). Alcohol (the Heineken document) is rising. Rejected: compounded or online-sourcing angles. Paused: efpeglenatide (Lane P, Korea-only). Other next-gen trial results (UBT251, CagriSema meta-analysis) go to Shorts only. Two things weren't verified: I couldn't fetch Lilly's release (403), so trial figures come from HCPLive and AJMC, and I couldn't count YouTube videos directly.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg (Ozempic's top dose) in type 2 diabetes: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, Oct 28 2026. 1,298 adults over 80 weeks. A1C −2.2 vs −1.8 points; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4%
candidates.angle: Lane C long-form, drug name first, e.g. 'Retatrutide vs Ozempic: What the New Trial Found' (≤50 characters). Open on 'you have type 2 diabetes and you're on semaglutide; here's what this trial means'. State that the figures assume everyone stayed on treatment, the result is not yet peer-reviewed, retatrutide is not approved, and this trial enrolled people with type 2 diabetes. Report discontinuation for side effects (4.8% and 7.9% vs 2.7%) and the GI effects. Skip 'first head-to-head' unless it's scoped exactly. If the held L1 10-29 covers this trial, fix it (masking, 'point', drug name) and publish it within the 48 h window rather than rewriting. Add 'don't switch medicines on your own' and the prescriber line.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–4 days (news peak Oct 28–30; YouTube search peak right after)
candidates.why_now: First reported Oct 28 10:45 UTC, so it's inside the 48 h Lane C window. Reuters, ABC, USA Today, NY Post, STAT, Fierce, BioSpace, AJMC, HCPLive and Everyday Health all ran it within 24 h. Retatrutide is our highest-peaking Shorts topic, and the format matches EloraTZP, our one proven spike.

evidence.signal: 1,298 randomized 2:2:1; A1C −2.2/−2.2 vs −1.8; weight −19.5%/−20.9% vs −9.4% at 80 weeks; efficacy estimand; discontinuation for side effects 4.8%/7.9% vs 2.7%; dysesthesia 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%; not yet published
